In-app and manual email routes tested.

Designated disposable-account checks passed for hosted deletion, shared progress, reconnect cleanup, and the manual email process. Testing has specific build and interruption limits. Read the tested scope.

1. Request account deletion by email

You can request deletion without reinstalling FitQuest. Email AustinMeridianHQ@gmail.com with the subject “FitQuest account and data deletion request.” State that you want your FitQuest account and associated personal data deleted. Where possible, write from the account’s registered email address.

Request deletion by email

This is a manual request to the Austin Meridian operator, operating as Austin Meridian. Opening the link does not send a message or delete an account automatically. Do not send your password, full save, backup codes, authentication tokens, recovery links, or identity documents.

Ownership verification and timing

The operator verifies ownership before removal. If you can sign in, the in-app current-password flow is preferred. For an email request, the manual procedure uses a fresh, single-use challenge sent to the registered address held in the account system, followed by your response and explicit deletion confirmation. A sender address, username, friend code, or screenshot alone is not proof of ownership.

If you cannot access the account or its registered inbox, explain that in your request so the operator can review available verification options. Removal cannot proceed by guessing who owns an account. After verification, the operator uses trusted account-management tools to remove the verified account through the same shared-data-preservation process.

Operating target: aim to finish verified requests within 30 days of receipt, resolving verification promptly and following applicable requirements. This is not an automated timer or a measured service guarantee. An owner-operated request, registered-address challenge, removal, and completion-email trial passed. The initial request reached the business Spam folder; delivery is not guaranteed. The operator monitors Inbox and Spam. Check your own Spam/Junk folder for our replies.

2. Delete your account in the updated app

These steps apply to builds containing the account-lifecycle screens. The operational report includes Android build-20 form/shared-deletion checks, Android build-21 installation and cleanup/restart checks, and current iPhone source in Expo Go. If your installed build lacks these controls, use the email route above.

  1. Go to Account → Account & Cloud Save → Your Account → Delete Account.
  2. Read the consequences. Connect to the internet and enter your current password in the app to verify ownership.
  3. Type DELETE, then choose Permanently Delete Account.

You can cancel before submission. Account deletion is permanent; do not treat a submitted request as cancellable. During submitted removal, the updated app stops gameplay and cloud sync for that account. The server operation removes live account records and preserves the shared progress described below. Once completion is confirmed, the app clears this account’s local copy on that device.

3. If deletion is interrupted

A lost connection or response does not prove that deletion failed or succeeded. The updated app keeps a pending marker and offers Check Status / Finish Cleanup to confirm completion or finish device cleanup. If completion cannot be confirmed, Retry Account Removal verifies the original account again using its password. Lost-response and retry behavior passed isolated automated tests. A physical phone interruption after verified submission was not deliberately reproduced, so not every interruption scenario is phone-verified.

Remove This Device Copy Only requires typing CLEAR LOCAL. It clears that account’s local copy and sign-in on the device. It does not confirm server deletion, cancel a submitted server request, or remove other accounts’ saves. If the app cannot safely identify the pending account, contact support.

4. What confirmed deletion removes

The updated implementation removes the following live data associated with the deleted account:

  • Authentication identity, associated sessions, and related legacy refresh-token records.
  • Both main and test cloud saves, private account/social profiles, and stored age band.
  • Personal friendships, blocks, requests, invitations, guild/raid memberships, and personal contribution, attack, and claim receipts.
  • Device push registrations and queued alerts to or from the account.

After server confirmation, this device’s account-specific main/test saves, pre-restore copies, conflict backups, cloud journals, playtest data, remembered credentials, offline markers, and local age choice clear. Local reminders and in-memory diagnostics are cleared by the updated flow. Other accounts’ saves remain. Hosted disposable-account checks showed the listed live Auth/private records removed from both cloud slots while the limited integrity marker remained. Functional phone checks confirmed signed-out restart and preservation of another account. Native file contents/removal were not directly inspected forensically; no production account was deleted for testing.

5. What can remain, and why

Shared progress

Remaining guild members keep de-identified workout, XP, and day counts without the removed account’s linkage. Leadership transfers to a surviving member; empty guilds disappear. In raids, remaining players’ progress, difficulty, rewards already claimed, and guardian health stay unchanged. Personal attack receipts are removed, but prior damage remains reflected in boss health. A party with no members can remain as unowned history.

Known attributable guild activity and name/email mentions in affected groups are removed or redacted. Arbitrary user-written text, screenshots, and copies held by others are not guaranteed discoverable or erasable.

Limited deletion records

An unlinked random-secret digest and completion time allow interrupted requests to check status for 30 days; they contain no account ID, email, or save. A separate restricted account-ID digest and completion timestamp support deletion integrity and backup recovery. This pseudonymous integrity record has a 12-month maintenance rule; it is not an anonymous record or a full save. Records start with the new migration and are not retroactive.

The daily hosted retention job was verified active with a successful scheduled execution. The expiry rules passed isolated mixed-age fixtures; newly created live records have not yet reached the full 30-day or 12-month lifetime. These results do not promise exact physical purge dates for every provider copy. No scheduled project backups or live provider-restoration service are currently provided. Any future restoration requires a separate restricted erasure log and reapplication before access reopens; that off-site recovery copy has not been established.

Manual records and outside copies

Minimal manual request records and resolved support email have owner-managed cleanup targets of 12 months after resolution, including completion of the deletion request. No automatic inbox cleanup or measured retention service is in place. These targets are separate from the implemented app/database rules.

Other offline devices cannot be remotely wiped. Updated signed-in devices check status on foreground and every 60 seconds, but cleanup requires server-confirmed deletion; old builds lack these controls. Exported backups/codes, screenshots, unlinked legacy copies, operating-system backups, provider logs/backups, and already handed-off notifications can remain outside immediate app control. Device/provider advertising and consent identifiers also have separate controls. The current Supabase Free Plan has no included scheduled project backups or point-in-time recovery. Its one-day API/database log and one-hour Auth audit-log access windows do not establish physical erasure of every underlying provider copy. No fixed universal provider expiry is promised. See the privacy retention disclosure.

6. Signing out or removing a device copy

Signing out ends remembered/offline account access on the device; it does not delete your online account, cloud saves, or local game progress. Uninstalling the app or clearing its storage can remove local data depending on the operating system, but does not itself remove server records or exported copies. Use account deletion or the manual email request route above for server-side removal.

7. Build availability and testing scope

The October 28, 2026 operational report supersedes earlier pending-status reports. Android 0.3.1/build 21 was built that evening and installed as an in-place update; startup, normal cleanup/restart, and survivor-account isolation passed owner checks. Earlier confirmation-form, cancellation, wrong-password, pre-verification outage, and shared-deletion checks used Android build 20 and current iPhone source in Expo Go. Expo Go has no standalone iPhone build number, and those earlier checks are not all build-21 tests.

Only designated disposable accounts were deleted. Hosted checks covered both cloud slots, the listed live Auth/private rows, the retained integrity marker, shared guild totals, raid health and contributions, and leadership transfer. The two-device test deleted an account online on iPhone while Android build 21 was offline; reconnecting Android returned it to sign-in and restart stayed signed out. Another account retained its shared progress. A very brief unidentified transition was accepted by the owner; this is not proof that no intermediate page rendered or that native files were forensically erased.

The manual email trial and current scheduled retention/push executions passed. The initial request reached Spam; a single successful trial is not a delivery guarantee or response-time SLA. Current push-worker success is not proof of a newly delivered notification. Physical post-submission interruption remains unverified, with isolated lost-response/retry coverage only.

The Supabase project is on the Free Plan in East US (North Virginia). The owner chose no project backups for now. Synthetic isolated recovery tests passed; a production/provider restore and separate encrypted off-site erasure-log copy were not demonstrated. No customer recovery-backup guarantee is provided. Live advertising and real FitQuest+ billing remain disabled.
